correctness.rationale: The product covariance integrations yield \(\operatorname{Var}(J)=3^{-d}\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(J,Y_x)=\prod_j(x_j-x_j^2/2)\), \(\operatorname{Var}(Y_x)=\prod_jx_j+\eta\). Gaussian regression reduces risk to one explicit nonnegative function. Its global maximum is interior; first-order equations enforce equality of all coordinates by strict monotonicity, and a one-crossing scalar equation gives unique global site. High-d bounds and log expansions yield the Lambert-W and crossover formulas. The standalone checker verifies finite covariance and root examples; those checks do not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: High-dimensional Bayesian quadrature with measurement noise has a substantive scale-selection problem: the noiseless point stays at \(2/3\) in every coordinate, but any fixed positive noise pushes the global optimum to a logarithmic corner boundary layer and accelerates the relative information decay from \((8/9)^d\) to \((3/4)^d/\eta\). The precise exponential-noise crossover gives a calibration law that cannot be obtained by simply tensoring one-dimensional noisy optimizers; it separates two physically meaningful sensing regimes.
